newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand chairman named to panel.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand chairman named to panel.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich Monday named MGM Grand Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Officer J. Terrence Lanni to be a member of the National Gambling Impact Commission.
Gingrich also named Kay James, dean of the Robertson School of Government at Regent University in Virgina Beach, Va., as a member of the nine-person panel.

The commission was established this year by Congress to make a two-year study of the effects of gambling on American society. Three members are to be named by President Clinton and three each by House and Senate leaders.
"With the selection of these two outstanding people, we will ensure that there is a balance of viewpoints represented on the commission," Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, said in a statement.
Lanni was with Caesars World Inc for 18 years before joining MGM Grand in 1995. Both companies operate casinos.

Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott had previously named James Dobson of Colorado, who heads a family focus organization, and Paul Moore, a Mississippi doctor, to the commission. House and Senate Democratic leaders will each choose one member of the panel.
